public_rationale: GPT-5 was released, and its launch evaluations recorded continuing factual errors and failures on missing-information tasks. Launch-day reporting also documented conspicuous basic text mistakes. Together these support the ordinary reading that hallucinations and multiple obvious errors would persist. OpenAI reported substantial improvements, so this does not establish unchanged reliability or a particular everyday failure rate.
limitations: The qualitative phrase a bunch of wacky errors requires interpretation.
Company evaluations are supplemented by news reporting rather than a complete independently reproduced test suite.
Results differ by mode and task.
Malformed image labels were excluded because a separate image model produced them.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: When GPT-5 is released, it will still hallucinate and make many wacky errors.

statement.excerpt: Gary Marcus is still betting that GPT-5 will continue to hallucinate and make a bunch of wacky errors, whenever it finally drops.
statement.document_title: GPT-5… now arriving Gate 8, Gate 9, Gate 10

from_speaker: make a bunch of wacky errors
our_interpretation: The release of GPT-5 is the antecedent.
Hallucination means generating false factual assertions as though they were true.
The plain reading of a bunch of wacky errors is recurring, conspicuous mistakes across prompts, without a specified population-wide error rate.
Assess the released GPT-5 system near launch. Improvements over predecessors are compatible with continuing errors.
Errors attributable solely to a separate image-generation model do not establish errors by GPT-5.
criteria.support_condition: After release, launch-era evaluations establish continuing hallucinations and multiple conspicuous errors across prompts attributable to GPT-5.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad, transparent launch-era evaluations establish that GPT-5 no longer hallucinates and does not exhibit recurring conspicuous mistakes, with purported examples shown to be invalid or misattributed.

evidence.locator: Closing availability paragraphs; page dated August 7, 2025
evidence.explanation: The dated rollout announcement establishes that GPT-5 was released, activating the forecast's condition.

evidence.locator: Opening discussion before What are hallucinations?
evidence.explanation: OpenAI explicitly confirms continuing GPT-5 hallucinations shortly after launch. It also states that their frequency has fallen.

evidence.locator: Hallucinations section, Figures 1–3; Deception section, Table 9
evidence.explanation: The launch card records nonzero factual-error rates across several evaluations; its missing-image test also records a 0.09 deception rate for GPT-5 thinking. These repeated failures support persistence, while the large reductions qualify any suggestion that reliability did not improve.

evidence.locator: Paragraph describing Guardian Australia's direct text test
evidence.explanation: The newsroom's test demonstrates an elementary counting error. The article also reports repeated blueberry letter-count errors and incorrect identification of US states containing R; these text examples supplement the primary evaluation evidence.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: After the release established by e1, documented elementary text failures supplemented the launch evaluation failures in e3, satisfying the rule for persistent hallucinations and repeated conspicuous errors.
